dashboard.loggedOutIntro1: SoundCarrot was born as a way to give my children a walled garden of curated content to explore, and then it just kind of, grew!

dashboard.yotoHeading: Yoto and SoundCarrot - you need to register with us to use the integration.
dashboard.yotoIntro1: Yoto is an amazing screen-free audio player for kids that uses cards to unlock stories, music, podcasts, and all kinds of fun audio adventures. One of its best features is the ability to make your own cards (MYO), so you can put exactly what your child loves onto their Yoto.
dashboard.yotoIntro2: They do this by letting you create custom cards from RSS feeds and podcasts, so you can turn any show into a personalised Make Your Own card - but you still need to find the feeds or episodes.
dashboard.yotoIntro3: Our new little 'add to Yoto' button lets you skip a step and send podcast episodes and curated playlists over with one click - but you do need to be logged in to our website.
dashboard.yotoIntro4: What you can do with SoundCarrot and Yoto is below. Want to register? The form is just up the page :)
dashboard.yotoBenefit1: Add any individual episode to your Yoto. Found a story, science nugget, or history gem your child will love? Just click “Send to Yoto” and drop that one episode straight into a Yoto Make Your Own playlist. Perfect for testing new shows or sharing a favourite moment.
dashboard.yotoBenefit2: Add one of our curated topic-based shows as a playlist. We group episodes into fun themes like Slime, Space, Unicorns, Amazing Inventions, and more, so you can send a whole bundle of related episodes to Yoto in one go. It feels like making your own custom “channel” around what your child is into right now.
dashboard.yotoBenefit3: Add one of our Curious Kids collections as a playlist. These are built around big question types: How, Who, and What. They're ideal for kids who love asking questions and discovering answers in short, punchy episodes.
dashboard.yotoBenefit4: When you click “Send to Yoto” you can choose an existing Yoto playlist or create a brand new one. Want a “Bedtime Stories” playlist? A “Science Saturdays” playlist? A “Maya's Favourites” playlist? You can build it exactly how you like, and keep adding to it over time.

home.heroH1: We love helping families find amazing children's podcasts.
home.heroBody1: At first I made this website for my kids - mostly to resolve the frustration my daughter experienced with mainstream podcast apps and the lack of easily discoverable age appropriate content - now I write the code and they act as curators, with nothing added without their say so.
home.heroBody2: Team Carrot is a father, a daughter, and a son, and we're building something that's gotten a little out of hand. We hope you like it :)

home.faqIntro: Straight answers about what SoundCarrot is, what it isn't, and how the carrot gets made.

faqs.a: SoundCarrot is a free directory of kids' podcasts, run by a dad and his kids. Every show is listened to and approved by the in-house curators (the kids) before it's added - nothing appears here without their say so.

faqs.q: Is it really free? Are there ads?
faqs.a: Completely free, and the site itself has no ads, banners or pop-ups. Some podcasts carry their own sponsor messages inside episodes - that's down to each show's creator, not us.
Every show is tagged as Under 5s, 6-10 or 11 plus, and you can filter by age on the shows page - or start from the age cards right here on the homepage.

faqs.q: How do you choose the shows?
faqs.a: The kids listen first. If it holds their attention and it's age-appropriate, it goes in. We also tag every show by topic, country and whether it's a serialised story or a dip-in-anywhere show.
No - everything is browsable and playable without one. A free account adds the nice-to-haves: tracking which episodes you've heard, liking episodes and saving favourite shows.

faqs.q: Why use this instead of our usual Podcast apps?
faqs.a: Those apps are built for adults, so kids' content is buried and recommendations wander off to who-knows-where. SoundCarrot only contains kid-approved shows, tells you which ones need to be heard in order, and always points you at episode one.

home.translationFaqQ: Is this page translated well? We're not native speakers!
home.translationFaqA: We're a small family doing our best - SoundCarrot's team speaks English at home, so pages in other languages are translated with care but without a native speaker checking every word. If something reads oddly or you spot a mistake, please let us know via our contact form and we'll fix it.
home.aboutBody1: We made this website primarily for my kids. A few years ago they gained a huge love of podcasts through shows like Finn Caspian, Becoming Mother Nature, Story Pirates and more. They grew environmentally conscious through Earth Rangers and Animal Sound Safari. And their critical thinking came on leaps and bounds thanks to the Big Fib. But finding good shows was hard, and I could never let my kids loose properly.
home.aboutBody2: SoundCarrot was born as a way to give them a walled garden of curated content, and a way to teach my daughter about writing code. A lot has changed since then.
